title: Freshworks Buys Robusta to Add AI Outage Investigation to Freshservice
excerpt: The undisclosed deal brings Robusta Dev's AI root-cause analysis into Freshservice, alongside FireHydrant, with engineers approving any production change.
body:
• Freshworks has acquired Israel-based Robusta Dev, an AI incident-investigation company, for an undisclosed amount.
  • Robusta's AI agents analyse monitoring data, infrastructure signals and recent code or configuration changes to find the cause of an outage and recommend fixes.
  • The technology will be integrated into Freshservice, Freshworks' IT service management platform, and linked with FireHydrant, its incident-response platform.
  • Engineers will review and approve recommended actions before any change touches production systems — human approval stays in the loop.

Freshworks has acquired Robusta Dev Ltd., an Israel-based company that uses AI to investigate technology outages, identify root causes and recommend remediation. The Nasdaq-listed software company announced the deal this week and said Robusta will strengthen Freshservice, its IT service management platform. Financial terms were not disclosed. The company's own announcement is published on The Works, Freshworks' company news site.

What Robusta does

Robusta, founded by Natan Yellin and Arik Alon, functions like an AI site reliability engineer. Its agents pull together monitoring data, infrastructure information and recent code or configuration changes, work out what caused a disruption, identify which connected services are affected and propose corrective steps. Freshworks said the system is built for very large enterprise environments, where the volume of raw events makes investigating each one individually prohibitively expensive in computing terms.

https://x.com/YourStoryCo/status/2115726647118975333

"Our technology lets AI Agents do that effectively in large enterprise environments, where there are so many raw events that investigating each one individually would be exorbitant from a token cost perspective."

— Natan Yellin, Co-founder and CEO, Robusta

Where it fits in Freshservice

The plan is to connect three stages that are usually separate: diagnosis in Robusta, service context in Freshservice — business services, system dependencies and change histories — and coordination in FireHydrant, the incident-management company Freshworks acquired last year. Findings and recommended actions are expected to surface in incident timelines and in tools such as Slack and Microsoft Teams. Freshworks said the aim is to move teams faster from identifying a problem to resolving it, and to use lessons from earlier outages to prevent repeats. The acquisition was reported by The Hindu BusinessLine and by Inc42.

A run of AI operations deals

Robusta is the latest in a sequence. Freshworks acquired FireHydrant in December last year to coordinate incident response, and earlier this month agreed to acquire Torii, a SaaS management platform that helps enterprises track software usage and govern AI spending. Robusta adds the missing first step in that chain: working out why something broke. Founded in Chennai in 2010 by Girish Mathrubootham and Shanmugam Krishnasamy, Freshworks sells cloud software for customer engagement, sales and IT service management. In the first quarter of 2026 it reported revenue up 16% year on year to $228.6 million and a net loss of $4.8 million, and announced plans to cut about 11% of its workforce, roughly 500 employees, as it increases its own use of AI in product development.

What to watch

The deal's test is integration, not announcement. Freshworks has not disclosed a price, a timeline for Robusta features to appear inside Freshservice, or how Robusta's existing customers will be handled. For IT teams — including the large Indian-origin engineering workforce that runs service operations for US enterprises — the practical question is whether automated root-cause analysis inside the service desk shortens outages measurably, or simply adds another AI layer to triage. Freshworks says engineers keep approval over production changes, which will be the feature enterprises in regulated industries examine first.
